introduction_markdown:
This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: answer ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: answer ALL TWO questions in this section. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3; if you attempt more than 2 questions, only the first 2 will be considered. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, Na = 23.0, Cu = 64.0, Cl = 35.5, K = 39.0, N = 14.0, S = 32.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give

(i) The atomic number of C.

(ii) The electronic configuration of D.

(iii) The electronic configuration of the ion of B. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) C has the configuration 2,8,4, so it has $2+8+4 = 14$ electrons. In a neutral atom the number of electrons equals the atomic number, so the atomic number of C is **14**.

(ii) D has atomic number 18, so 18 electrons: **2,8,8**.

(iii) B has atomic number 12, so its configuration is 2,8,2. It has two electrons in its outer shell and loses them to form the ion $\mathrm{B^{2+}}$, whose configuration is **2,8**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of these elements does not form compounds? Give a reason for your answer.

Element: ........

Reason: ........ *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Element: D.**

Reason: D (atomic number 18, configuration 2,8,8) has a **completely filled outer shell** (a stable octet). It does not need to gain, lose or share electrons, so it does not combine with other elements. It is a noble gas (argon).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Which of the elements is a halogen?

(ii) Write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction between hydrogen and the halogen in (c)(i). *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **E.** Its configuration is 2,8,7: seven electrons in the outer shell, so it is in Group VII (the halogens). With atomic number 17, E is chlorine.

(ii) Hydrogen reacts with chlorine to form hydrogen chloride:

$\mathrm{H_2} + \mathrm{Cl_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{HCl}$

Check: 2 H and 2 Cl on each side.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Write the formula of the compound formed between B and E.

(ii) Identify the bond type in the compound formed in (d)(i). *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) B loses 2 electrons to form $\mathrm{B^{2+}}$; E gains 1 electron to form $\mathrm{E^{-}}$. Two $\mathrm{E^{-}}$ ions are needed to balance one $\mathrm{B^{2+}}$, so the formula is **$\mathrm{BE_2}$** (magnesium chloride, $\mathrm{MgCl_2}$).

(ii) **Ionic (electrovalent) bond**: electrons are transferred from the metal B to the non-metal E, and the oppositely charged ions attract each other.
